newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Guatemala against backing Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China warns Guatemala against backing Taiwan.

text.p: China warned Guatemala on Thursday against supporting its rival, Taiwan, but stopped short of saying whether it would veto a United Nations plan to send a peacekeeping mission to the Central American country.
"It is regretful... It grossly interferes in China's internal affairs," Chinese Foreign Minstry spokesman Shen Guofang said of Guatemala's support for Taiwan's bid to rejoin the United Nations.
"It will seriously destroy the political foundation for cooperation between China and Guatemala in the United Nations," Shen told a news briefing.
Shen did not elaborate on what he meant by U.N. cooperation between China and Guatemela.
Guatemala has diplomatic relations with Taiwan but not China.
Last week, China baulked at the U.N. plan to send military observers to Guatelama to implement a new peace agreement aimed at ending more than three decades of civil war, U.N. diplomats have said.

Beijing told Security Council members that Guatemala's actions threatened China's "territorial integrity", an apparent reference to the Central American country's support of moves aimed at securing membership for Taiwan in the United Nations.
China replaced Taiwan in the world body in 1971. The two have been diplomatic rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Shen said Guatemala must "rectify its erroneous policy and adopt constructive measures to create the necessary atmosphere and condition to appropriately resolve problems".
But Shen stopped short of saying whether China would veto the sending of U.N. peacekeepers to Guatemala.
Shen criticised Guatemala for inviting Taiwan's foreign minister, John Chang, to attend the signing of the peace settlement on December 29.

In Taipei on Thursday, Chang said Taiwan would continue its quest to join the United Nations, despite China's objections, but conceded it may have to settle initially for U.N. observer status before again seeking full entry into the United Nations.
China regards Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation.
